headline: Last session: Indian markets snapped two-week gains as surging crude oil prices and heavy FPI outflows weighed

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: FPIs withdrew ₹48,056 crore from Indian equities in October amid elevated crude oil prices.
Surging oil prices rallying towards $116 dragged Indian shares to weekly losses.
Geopolitical uncertainty escalated as US threats against Iran fueled fears of oil supply disruptions.
Selling pressure in key sectors like auto, FMCG, and IT dragged Sensex and Nifty lower in recent sessions.
whatHappening: On the last trading session, Nifty closed at 22,600 and Sensex fell 125 points, snapping two-week gains.
LKP's Vatsal Bhuva noted Swiggy may rebound to Rs 190, though charts do not yet signal a trend reversal.
L&T Tech and Shriram Finance are among 24 stocks turning ex-record date this week for dividends and stock splits.
Market participants are monitoring the grey market premium ahead of Jio's mega IPO listing this week.
summary: In the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-week winning streak as Sensex and Nifty logged weekly losses under pressure from surging crude oil prices and massive FPI outflows of ₹48,056 crore in October. Corporate action remains high with 24 stocks like L&T Tech and Shriram Finance turning ex-record date this week alongside Jio's mega IPO listing. Markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 26 October.
